subject: Physics
description: Conduction, convection, radiation; thermos flask; greenhouse effect; sea breeze

questions.stem: Heat is transferred through SOLIDS primarily by which mechanism?

options.option_text: Convection due to fluid flow across the solid
Conduction by lattice vibrations and free electrons
Radiation by infrared waves moving inside the solid
Evaporation of moisture trapped within the solid

questions.explanation: CONDUCTION — heat flows from hot to cold parts of a solid via lattice vibrations (phonons) and, in metals, free-electron motion. No bulk movement of matter. Metals are good conductors because they have many free electrons. CONVECTION (Distractor 1) — works in fluids (liquids/gases) via bulk flow. RADIATION (Distractor 3) — does pass through transparent media but isn't the main mode in opaque solids. Distractor 4 — evaporation is irrelevant to solid heat transfer.

questions.stem: A SEA BREEZE that blows from sea to land during the day is the result of:

options.option_text: Differential conduction of heat through solid earth and water
Convection — land heats faster, hot air rises, cooler air rushes in
Radiation imbalance between the sunlit land and the sunlit sea
Evaporation directly cooling the moist air over the open sea

questions.explanation: Land has lower specific heat than water → heats faster during the day. Air over land becomes hot, rises (low pressure forms). Cooler air over sea (high pressure) flows in to replace it → SEA BREEZE during the day. At night, the reverse — land cools faster → land high pressure → LAND BREEZE blows from land to sea. Both are CONVECTION-driven. Distractor 1 — conduction in earth is too slow. Distractor 3 — radiation difference contributes but the moving air is convection. Distractor 4 — evaporation cools but doesn't drive the breeze.

questions.stem: A THERMOS FLASK keeps liquids hot or cold for hours by minimising:

options.option_text: Only conduction of heat from the contents to outside
Conduction, convection AND radiation all together by design
Only radiation through the silvery inner walls of the flask
Only convection by sealing the lid tightly during use

questions.explanation: Thermos / Dewar flask defeats all three modes: (1) DOUBLE WALL with VACUUM between → no conduction or convection through the gap (no medium to carry heat). (2) SILVERED INNER SURFACES → reflect infrared radiation back. (3) Insulated stopper / lid → reduces conduction at the top. Even so, slow loss occurs (a real-life vacuum isn't perfect). Invented by Sir James Dewar (1892) for cryogenic liquids. Distractors 1, 3, 4 each name only ONE mechanism; the answer is all three.

questions.stem: The GREENHOUSE EFFECT on Earth is caused by:

options.option_text: Direct conduction of heat from the sun's surface
Atmospheric gases trapping outgoing infrared radiation
Convection currents in the upper atmosphere
Volcanic eruptions on the planet's surface

questions.explanation: Earth absorbs short-wavelength sunlight, re-radiates it as longer-wavelength INFRARED. Greenhouse gases (CO₂, water vapour, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone) absorb this IR and re-emit some back toward Earth → surface stays warmer than it would in a transparent atmosphere. Without GHG: Earth would average ~−18 °C (uninhabitable). With natural GHG: ~+15 °C (just right). Anthropogenic CO₂ rise from ~280 ppm (pre-industrial) to >420 ppm today is enhancing the effect → global warming. Distractor 1 — conduction doesn't operate across vacuum of space. Distractor 3 — convection is irrelevant to this. Distractor 4 — volcanism is a smaller separate factor.

questions.stem: Why are cooking utensils made of materials like ALUMINIUM and COPPER but with WOODEN handles?

options.option_text: Wood looks attractive while metal is durable for cooking
Metal conducts heat well to food while wood insulates the hand
Wood is cheaper than metal, reducing manufacturing cost
Wood is heavier than metal, so it stays steady on stove

questions.explanation: Metals (Cu, Al, steel) — high thermal conductivity → quickly transfer stove heat to food. Wood (and modern plastics) — low conductivity → handle stays cool enough to grip safely. The combination optimises function: efficient cooking + safe handling. Distractor 1 — aesthetics aren't the engineering reason. Distractor 3 — cost is incidental. Distractor 4 — wood is generally LIGHTER than metal, not heavier.

questions.stem: Why is the BOTTOM of a cooking pot painted BLACK and the OUTSIDE often kept SHINY?

options.option_text: Black bottom looks elegant and shiny outside reflects oil splatter
Black absorbs heat efficiently from the flame; shiny reduces heat loss
Both are purely cosmetic features unrelated to thermal physics
Black paint and shiny finish are both heat resistant materials

questions.explanation: BLACK surfaces are good ABSORBERS of radiation (black-body). The pot's bottom blackens with carbon over time; this enhances absorption of radiative + flame heat → faster cooking. SHINY (polished metal) surfaces are poor absorbers AND poor emitters → reduce radiative heat loss from the pot's outside to the kitchen. Result: more energy goes into the food, less is wasted. Stefan-Boltzmann law governs radiative heat: Q = εσA(T⁴ − T_amb⁴), where ε (emissivity) is high for black, low for polished. Distractor 1, 3 are aesthetic non-explanations. Distractor 4 — heat resistance isn't the mechanism.

questions.stem: A black body is a body that:

options.option_text: Reflects all incident radiation back to its source
Absorbs all incident radiation across all wavelengths
Emits radiation only at one specific wavelength only
Has zero emission of thermal radiation at all temperatures

questions.explanation: BLACK BODY — idealised body that absorbs ALL incident electromagnetic radiation (no reflection, no transmission). At thermal equilibrium, by Kirchhoff's law of radiation, it also EMITS the maximum possible radiation for its temperature → the spectrum follows Planck's distribution. Stars approximate black bodies; the cosmic microwave background is a near-perfect black body at 2.725 K. Wien's law: peak wavelength × T = constant. Hotter stars peak in blue/UV, cooler stars in red/IR. Distractor 1 = white body / mirror. Distractor 3 = laser / monochromatic emitter. Distractor 4 = unphysical at any T > 0.
